title: Frobenius Algebras and Oriented Two-Dimensional Sewing

items.title: The oriented open-closed surface category with colored free boundary
items.statement: Define the boundary-relative symmetric monoidal category of compact oriented smooth surfaces with black incoming/outgoing circles and intervals, S-colored free boundary, corners, and face-compatible collars; define its no-free-boundary closed subcategory.
items.strategy: Specify objects, morphisms, relative equivalence, gluing, tensor, symmetry, collars, and the closed subcategory with all boundary and endpoint conventions.
items.axiom_base: ACω is used only for global smooth collar existence; collar choices and all algebraic definitions are explicit.

items.title: Frobenius objects and typed colored knowledgeable sewing data
items.statement: Define finite-dimensional Frobenius-object data over an arbitrary field, symmetric and commutative as distinct properties, singleton knowledgeable data (A,C,i,i*), the full S-colored objects A_ab and typed equations (5.2)–(5.14), and structure-preserving morphisms.
items.strategy: Give every map's source and target, include associators and unitors, and state all algebra, coalgebra, Frobenius, symmetry, centrality, duality, Cardy, and morphism equations.
items.axiom_base: No choice; all vector spaces are finite-dimensional over an arbitrary field k.

items.title: A Frobenius functional determines a unique Frobenius coproduct
items.statement: For any finite-dimensional unital k-algebra with nondegenerate form ε(ab), construct the basis-independent inverse-pairing tensor, define Δ(a)=(a⊗1)e, and prove both counits, coassociativity and both Frobenius identities; conversely, Frobenius-object axioms give nondegenerate pairing by the two snake identities.
items.strategy: Use a left/right dual basis for the possibly nonsymmetric pairing, identify its inverse tensor intrinsically, transpose multiplication under the perfect pairing, and derive both snake identities in the converse direction.
items.axiom_base: Choice-free finite-dimensional linear algebra over k; no characteristic or semisimplicity hypothesis.

items.title: Face-relative Morse decomposition into the ten sewing generators
items.statement: Under ACω, every compact oriented open-closed surface with parametrized black boundary, S-colored free boundary, and corners admits a face-compatible excellent Morse function whose regular-level cuts decompose it into identities and the ten typed generators μ_A,η_A,Δ_A,ε_A,μ_C,η_C,Δ_C,ε_C,i,i*; every mixed interior saddle factors into those generators.
items.strategy: Construct compatible collars and a boundary-relative function; make its free-face restrictions Morse, perturb in finitely many interior charts, separate the finite critical values, and analyze each local index/sign case.
items.axiom_base: ACω is required through the collar and parametric-transversality suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

items.title: The finite basic sewing relations hold relative to all boundary labels
items.statement: Prove the closed commutative-Frobenius relations, open symmetric-Frobenius relations, zipper algebra and centrality relations, cozipper duality, and the typed Cardy equation as actual boundary-relative diffeomorphisms of the exact S-colored surface category.
items.strategy: For each relation, cut both surfaces along stated seam arcs to oriented disks, match all edge and marked-boundary words, extend over the disks, and smooth in fixed seam collars; treat Cardy as the same genus-zero annular strip with its two black intervals in the same cyclic order.
items.axiom_base: Choice-free finite topological verification once the collars are fixed; all boundary colors are preserved.

items.title: Algebraic derivations of the sewing moves
items.statement: Derive both snake identities, symmetry and invariance of pairings and copairings, both zipper/cozipper transports, cozipper coalgebra preservation, open and closed window and handle slides, Cardy consequences, and cyclic cozipper rotation, with all S-color indices typed.
items.strategy: Expand every move as a typed linear composite, use Frobenius associativity/unit/counit, transpose under the nondegenerate pairings, and cancel the two snakes.
items.axiom_base: Choice-free algebra over k, with no characteristic, symmetry-to-commutativity, or semisimplicity shortcut.

items.title: The marked boundary-relative open-closed normal word
items.statement: Define a deterministic typed normal word for each connected colored surface from its marked black-boundary cycles, their endpoint colors and cyclic orders, genus, and number of free windows of each color; specify empty source/target conventions and marked-slot permutations.
items.strategy: Give the formal word after bending open and closed boundary slots with the pairings and copairings; treat it as a candidate normal word until the dependent lemma proves independence and completeness.
items.axiom_base: No new axiom; its well-definedness is discharged by the named local normal-form lemma under that lemma's ACω hypothesis.

items.title: The complete colored boundary-relative surface normal-form theorem
items.statement: Every connected S-colored open-closed surface word reduces by the locally proved sewing relations to the candidate normal word; equality holds exactly when the marked component partition, genus, colored free-window counts, open-boundary cycles, and endpoint color sequences agree. Include components with empty black boundary and prove the disconnected tensor case.
items.strategy: Follow all LP stages I–XI: remove open extrema; normalize open multiplication by bounded vertex-height; restart after each strict outer reduction; eliminate zippers; normalize closed multiplication and comultiplication; order windows and handles; then discharge empty-boundary cases. Prove every local move algebraically before use.
items.axiom_base: ACω only through face-relative Morse decomposition; finite algebraic reductions and termination measures use no further choice.

items.title: Closed oriented two-dimensional TQFTs are commutative Frobenius algebras
items.statement: For the closed oriented surface category with no free boundary at all, symmetric monoidal functors to Vect_fd(k) and monoidal natural transformations are equivalent to finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebras and maps preserving all Frobenius data. Give the connected genus-g map formula, empty source/target conventions, spheres, and disconnected surfaces.
items.strategy: Extract μ,η,Δ,ε from four closed generators; verify the relations; construct the reverse functor by the proved closed normal form and show the correspondence on objects, maps, and monoidal natural transformations.
items.axiom_base: Arbitrary field k; ACω is inherited only from the surface normal-form supplier.

items.title: Typed colored knowledgeable Frobenius data classify open-closed sewing
items.statement: For arbitrary S and arbitrary field k, symmetric monoidal functors from the exact S-colored open-closed surface category to Vect_fd(k), with monoidal natural transformations, are equivalent to the S-colored knowledgeable Frobenius data of the stated typed equations. Prove the singleton (A,C,i,i*) case and the closed sector without identifying C with Z(A).
items.strategy: Extract maps from all ten generators and verify every relation; reverse by any finite decomposition, use the normal-form theorem for independence, and identify homomorphisms with monoidal natural transformations on generators.
items.axiom_base: Arbitrary field k and arbitrary color set S; ACω is inherited only from face-relative surface normal forms; no semisimplicity or C=Z(A).

title: Frobenius Algebras and Oriented Two-Dimensional Sewing: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The dual numbers are symmetric Frobenius and nonsemisimple over every field
items.statement: For every field k, A=k[x]/(x²) with ε(1)=0 and ε(x)=1 has pairing matrix [[0,1],[1,0]], coproduct Δ(1)=1⊗x+x⊗1 and Δ(x)=x⊗x; verify all Frobenius identities and prove that A is not a semisimple algebra.
items.strategy: Compute on the basis 1,x, check coassociativity and all four basis-pair Frobenius cases, then show the only simple left submodule is kx and cannot sum to A.
items.axiom_base: Choice-free and valid in every characteristic, including characteristic two.

references.title: Joachim Kock, Frobenius algebras and 2D topological quantum field theories, complete minicourse notes
Aaron D. Lauda and Hendryk Pfeiffer, Open-closed strings: Two-dimensional extended TQFTs and Frobenius algebras, arXiv:math/0510664v3

items.title: A nonabelian group algebra is symmetric Frobenius but not a closed sector
items.statement: For every field k, k[S₃] is symmetric Frobenius by the coefficient-of-identity form and is noncommutative because (12)(23)≠(23)(12); therefore it cannot itself be the commutative algebra assigned to a circle by a closed oriented 2D TQFT, though this does not rule out a separate knowledgeable open/closed extension.
items.strategy: Use the actual any-field statement of the published symmetric-pairing proposition, compute two products in the group basis, and apply only the closed-sector commutativity conclusion.
items.axiom_base: Choice-free over every field; no assertion that a symmetric algebra automatically extends to knowledgeable open/closed data.
